event.summary: Check explicit acceptance of ending old terminals on upgrade
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Starting the upgraded supervisor ends terminals created by older releases, including running agents and shell tabs, and their retained output is no longer available.

Details: Assigned patch lines 101-111 replaces preservation of old tmux terminals with ending them at startup; lines 429-501 remove the history-preserving tmux-to-host Restart path. SPEC_impl.md:2880 onward describes startup termination and conversion to interrupted. Need check complete governing SPEC.md terminal/upgrade contracts and implementation startup route to distinguish intended breaking behavior from an unauthorized loss-of-work change. Suggested bucket: potentially highest (processes and retained terminal work). Confidence: source-confirmed design; contract acceptance not yet fully checked. Could-be-highest: yes. proposed_drop: false pending contract review. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. No runtime behavior observed and no reproduction requested.

event.summary: Proposed drop: ending old terminals is explicitly specified
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: The upgraded supervisor stops agents and shell tabs still in old tmux terminals and loses their retained screen and scrollback; subsequent Restart starts an empty terminal. This could otherwise be loss of user-owned processes/work.

Details: Assigned SPEC_impl.md patch lines 101-111 states that old tmux terminals end at startup; lines 429-501 remove the history-preserving tmux-to-host Restart path. The complete SPEC.md Terminal experience section at the same revision explicitly requires this breaking behavior, at lines 3003-3016: "This release ends them: the first time a host's supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program." It continues: "one whose agent had already ended keeps its outcome, but its terminal's last screen, which lived in the server, is gone; old tabs are closed." It also says: "After an update to this release, Restart, Clone and Replace start such a session in a new, empty terminal." SPEC_impl.md:2880-2930 describes the replacement cleanup/conversion contract. Suggested bucket: highest if unintended, because the consequence includes terminating user-owned processes and losing retained output; could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source/contract acceptance, not runtime-observed. proposed_drop: explicit product specification acceptance quoted above; preserve for independent highest-drop check. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: this excludes independent cleanup ownership or implementation failures, which are not excused merely by the intended migration. Revision closes the initial lead by establishing the missing acceptance premise.

event.summary: Check rewritten terminal switch-point reference against removed type
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: The implementation specification may direct future changes to a terminal abstraction that this commit deletes, obscuring where terminal behavior now belongs.

Details: Assigned patch lines 125-126 rewrites the switch-point description as `service/terminals.rs`'s `Terminal`, now described as a host runtime. The pinned service/terminals.rs header and first 180 lines instead identify and return `HostTerminal`, imported from hosts, with no `Terminal` shown. Need inspect the whole file's definitions and actual host methods to settle whether a compatibility alias exists or the architecture pointer is stale. Suggested bucket: other, documentation correctness. Could-be-highest: no; no established security or loss-of-work route from this developer pointer. Confidence: unresolved source lead. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. No execution observed.

event.summary: Rewritten terminal contract points to the deleted Terminal type
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Developers following the authoritative implementation specification are directed to a terminal type and implementation location that no longer exist, making the new terminal ownership and safety behavior harder to find. This is documentation drift, with no demonstrated runtime effect.

Details: SPEC_impl.md:2210-2211 (assigned patch lines 125-126) explicitly rewrites the switch-point map to say `service/terminals.rs`'s `Terminal` is now a host runtime. The same commit deletes that enum and its dispatch implementation from crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/terminals.rs; the new module imports HostTerminal at line 13 and resolve_terminal returns it at lines 122-128. Whole-file git grep -w Terminal at the reviewed revision found only the English word in the module header, and no alias or type. The actual runtime is HostTerminal in crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/hosts/terminal.rs:1226, with status at 2113, evidence at 2539, sweep_root at 2571 and wire_kind/tab_info at 2641/2648. The contract should name HostTerminal and its actual module, retaining service/terminals.rs only for identity resolution and attachment bookkeeping. Suggested bucket: other (incorrect developer-facing architecture pointer). Confidence: confirmed through pinned source and the per-commit deletion, not execution. Could-be-highest: no; no established security or loss-of-work route from this pointer. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Material caveat: behavior described in the rest of the paragraph may still be correct; the finding concerns the stale abstraction/location newly presented as the replacement architecture. Revision closes f2's alias-existence check.

event.summary: Removed tmux pause and sink mechanics belong to the retired producer
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333

TLDR: Removing the old pause/sink explanation does not by itself change a viewer's output retention or let a slow viewer block another terminal; the current supervisor serves terminal-host grids instead.

Details: Assigned patch lines 19-85 removes tmux pause-after, per-session sink and xterm/tmux retention-size details. Considered whether this removes a live flow-control safety invariant. Refuted by the replacement at SPEC_impl.md:1748-1753, which explicitly scopes byte-stream mechanics to earlier supervisors, and by the complete Terminal host / Grid streams contract (SPEC_impl.md:2627 onward): a paused grid sender reads the emulator's current screen and sends retained history, independently of the terminal host consuming the program's output. Pinned crates/farhelm-supervisor/src/service/terminals.rs:1-9 identifies HostTerminal as the only backing runtime, resolve_terminal returns HostTerminal, and service/connection.rs:8-9 identifies the output side as the grid sender. The old driver's sink-specific mechanism is no longer an implementation obligation for a current terminal. No independent source route to lost work was established from deleting this explanatory text. Suggested bucket: other, if documentation incompleteness had remained; could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work premise from this deletion, distinct from f1's explicitly accepted terminal shutdown. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of this concern; not runtime-observed. proposed_drop: source refutation above; no live tmux producer remains at the reviewed revision. possible_cover: none. Material caveat: existing older supervisors retain their own implementation and must still satisfy the byte-stream product contract; this review did not re-audit retired code for unrelated bugs.

event.summary: Old-terminal retry documentation omits retained allocated checkouts
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. In-range introduction: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513.

TLDR: The implementation specification tells maintainers that an old-terminal create retry is rolled back when refused, but an earlier attempt that already allocated its checkout deliberately keeps a visible error session and its ownership records. This is inaccurate failure-lifecycle documentation; the inspected implementation preserves the checkout correctly.

Details: Assigned patch lines 280-287 rewrites/reflows the Creating agents in hosts paragraph. At the reviewed source SPEC_impl.md:2258-2259 it says a row the takeover claims is refused before anything starts and "rolled back like a launch whose spec never landed", with its refusal settled against the intent key, without the allocated-checkout distinction. core.rs:14700-14763 implements two different outcomes: no checkout or a still-Planned checkout can roll back; an allocated or unreadable checkout calls retain_create_refusal and keeps the session and checkout records. The source contract explicitly states why: deleting the last ownership record would orphan the checkout. Ordinary post-allocation failure handling at core.rs:11104-11112 likewise explicitly calls its retained-refusal path "not a rollback". Product contract SPEC.md:1757 says exactly: "Once allocation has occurred, failures retain the session and its checkout association for inspection and Delete." SPEC_impl.md:3807-3809 says: "A post-allocation failure atomically retains an error session and membership instead of losing the only deletion handle." Those correct governing statements make the blanket retry-rollback wording inconsistent; production correctness does not refute the distinct documentation defect. Clarify the retry paragraph with the same pre-allocation/allocated distinction as the helper.

Attribution checked across the pinned range: the exclusive base has no retried-tmux/takeover rollback assertion in SPEC_impl.md. git log -S identifies 647f0227 as its introduction (then SPEC_impl.md:2315-2319); that revision's core.rs:15854-15925 already implements and documents the allocated-checkout retention branch. Thus predating 1ed482d does not put the defect outside the review range; 1ed482d retains it in this assigned rewrite. The concern is not a new runtime regression at either revision.

Suggested bucket: other (documentation contract accuracy). Confidence: confirmed by source, governing contracts and full-range attribution; no runtime behavior observed. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this prose; the current runtime explicitly retains user work and its deletion handle. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none found in the supplied interface context; no prohibited coverage sources searched. Caveats: ordinary non-checkout retry rollback is correct; the defect is the omitted allocated-checkout exception, not the refusal itself, the existence of a terminal-host replacement, or the accepted retirement consequence. This revision closes f4's rollback-terminology lead under its original ID.
